## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bcdc77c8216f5b2344c71b79e85b8acd8ee02133`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher-membership-vetted-organization.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/admitting-credential.ts, packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/admission-tenancy-posture.ts, packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts, packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx, content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher-membership-resolved-principal.test.ts, .changeset/environment-membership-vetted-organization.md (read for ②)

Inputs: the PR body, its two commits and their messages, the four-path net diff against `main` (merge-base `4cd48e277`; `main` has since moved to `dabef0f66` with no change to any cited file), the check-runs on the head, the published spec and the cited code on `main`, and the drafter's private hand-back, whose claims were checked against the tree. No card, by the maintainer's ruling for this series; `Refs #28284` is the series mailbox, closed, with nothing on it about this PR. Why line, as fixed: 「QA 第三轮发现的安全加固(细节按披露裁决不公开)」.

Check-runs on the head at the time of writing: 47 runs, 43 completed (30 `success`, 13 `skipped`, none failed, none cancelled), 4 still in progress (`Test Core` shards 1 to 4). Among the completed successes: `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` shards 5 to 8, every `Type Check` family (`workspace`, `source gates`, `consumer gates`, `debt ledger`), every `Lint` family (`ESLint`, `docs & code guards`, `repo & tooling gates`, `CI, release & engine gates`, `PM dispatch-gates`, both `scoped` families and `tooling self-tests`), `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts this record relies on; the verdict below stands on the diff and the completed runs, the seat gates landing on the remaining four shards finishing green, and a red run reopens this record.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of the dispatcher's scoped routes on a multi-environment host, for a caller a session cookie admitted.** `HttpDispatcher.enforceProjectMembership` (http-dispatcher.ts 1519-1750 on the head) runs after `resolveRequestScope` (dispatch() 2871) and the ADR-0069 gate, and before every domain body (2888), on every route except the control-plane skip list, the share-link resolve and messages routes, the exact approvals act route, the inbound hook `POST`, requests with no `environmentId` and the system environment. For a session-admitted caller, the organization the platform-organization pass reads is now `executionContext.tenantId` (1651-1653), read only when `executionContext.userId` is the user the gate's own session read names. A session caller whose resolution carries no organization, or with no resolution of that user on the request, has no organization read and is judged on `sys_environment_member` like any other caller; the refusal is unchanged (`403`, `code: PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED`, `details: { environmentId, userId }` naming the session's user, as `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx` 455-463 documents it). **Right** against the published contract on `main`: `api.enforceProjectMembership` is declared as the "Per-environment membership 403 gate (dispatcher)" (stack.zod.ts 1074); `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx` 109 puts every request an environment resolves "behind the same project-membership and capability gates"; the pass itself is declared for members of the platform organization (`PLATFORM_ORG_ID`, 466-467); and the organization a session principal acts in is, by the one rule the repository publishes for every door, the one the request's resolution answers (`resolveActiveOrganizationId` docblock 2448-2484; `metaCallerOrganizationId`, meta-item-read-gate.ts 232-253; the #15409 ruling B block at resolve-authz-context.ts 734-815).
2. **The value read is the one every other door reads.** `executionContext.tenantId` for a session principal is written by `resolveAuthzContext` (resolve-authz-context.ts 671, with 795-815 deciding what it holds) and copied by the shared assembler (assemble-execution-context.ts 374); `resolveActiveOrganizationId` reads that same field through `metaCallerOrganizationId`. One source, no second vetting path added. **Right.**
3. **The same-user guard.** The pass reads the resolution only when its `userId` equals the user of the gate's session read. A resolution carrying no `userId` (the guest envelope, assemble-execution-context.ts 373 and 433) or another user's reads nothing. In production both reads are the same `getSession` on the same request headers (request-execution-context.ts 246-254 feeding resolve-authz-context.ts 636-637; the gate at 1626-1631), so they agree for every session caller; where they could not, the gate judges, which is the fail-closed side. **Right**, and load-bearing: without the guard a guest envelope's derived organization would be readable here.
4. **Unchanged, verified by reading.** The API-key and OAuth arms (`admittingCredentialKind` at 1643-1646, #31396) are reached before the new `else` and still read the resolution's user and organization; the `sessionUnread` fail-open (1647-1649) and the anonymous return (1652) are unchanged; hosts with no `kernel-resolver` (no `environmentId`, return at 1611) and hosts with `api.enforceProjectMembership: false` (1524) are unchanged; the skip list, the three token-is-the-authorisation exemptions, the system environment, the positive-membership cache keyed `environment:user` and the refusal shape are unchanged. A session naming an organization other than the platform one was judged before and is judged now. A host with no tenancy wall (`single` posture, or no `tenancy` service) answers the same organization for a session as before (`vetOrganizationClaim`, resolve-authz-context.ts 855-864), so its accept set does not move. **Right.**
5. **Public surface: unchanged.** No export, type or schema moves; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
6. **Pins.** The new file drives `dispatch()` through the real identity step (`resolveRequestScope` to `resolveAuthzContext`, `tenancy: { posture: 'isolated' }` read by `effectiveTenancyPosture`, api-key.ts 596-601) on a stub multi-tenant host whose `sys_environment_member` holds no row: a session judged in the organization its resolution answers (refused, one membership read for that user); CONTROL, a member of the platform organization passes with no read; CONTROL, a session in another organization the user is in is judged. The RBAC block in `http-dispatcher.test.ts` hands the platform-pass case the resolution as `dispatch()` writes it, and the new case pins the three no-organization shapes (no resolution, another user's resolution, a resolution with no organization) each judged with a membership read for the session's user. The module-top `import '@objectstack/metadata'` in that file is the `check:test-source-alias` requirement; test-only. The red-first (2 failed | 253 passed against `main`'s blob) and restore (263/263) readings in the PR body are consistent with the tree; not reproduced (read-only).

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/runtime`: patch.** Right: a bug fix in a released package, no protocol kind, and `skip-changeset` would have been wrong.
- **`Clause-②: no` — correctly `no`, not `no (narrowing)`.** The capability the package declares is the per-environment membership gate on scoped routes, with a pass for members of the platform organization. The organization a session principal is in is, on `main`, one published fact for every door: the one its resolution answers (①1, ①2). Nothing on `main` promises a session caller whose resolution answers no organization a scoped route in an environment it is not a member of; what this PR refuses is that caller, with the same remedy every other caller has (membership in the environment). That is the spec's own refusal delivered at the one door that had not yet read the shared answer, not a declared capability taken away at the consumer. No author-writable thing is removed or renamed, so there is no FROM-to-TO migration to carry. #31396, the precedent the PR cites, brought the API-key and OAuth arms of this same gate to the same source and was judged `no` at `patch` by this reviewer's record, on this basis; #31263 and #31320 in this series were landed on it too. The record is nonetheless rendered on the narrowing face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, so the scrutiny a `no (narrowing)` would owe was applied (④). Both declaration lines are present and identical in the PR body and the changeset; the changeset body names the package, the level, which callers the check now reads differently, which are unchanged, and the two unchanged host postures. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` on the head: success.
- **Disclosure check.** The PR title and body (both languages), the changeset body, the new source comment, the new test file's header and case names, the modified test's comment and the second commit's message were read. All stay at the level of behaviour: which callers are judged, which are not, where the check sits, what value it reads and what the refusal answers, plus the maintainer's fixed why line. No breach on the head's tree or on the PR. **One breach in the first commit's body** (`ad7e2590`): its second sentence contrasts the organization the check now reads with the one it read before and names that former input. That names what the check used to read, which the ruling keeps off the record. The second commit removed the same contrast from the changeset, the test header, one test name and the source comment, so the head's tree is clean and the first commit's body is the only carrier. **Should-fix S2:** the seat lands the PR squashed, with a squash body taken from the PR title plus the changeset paragraph (or the body's "What changes" bullet), which carry no such contrast, so the merged history holds no commit body naming it and does not hold the first commit's intermediate tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Flag: "Clause-② no, patch, on the #31396 precedent; flag the narrowing reading to the seat."** Answered in ②: `no` stands.
- **Flag: under postures with no tenancy wall the value read equals what was read before, so no change there.** Confirmed in the tree (①4, `vetOrganizationClaim`).
- **Flag: only the session arm moves; the API-key and OAuth arms already read the resolution (#31396).** Confirmed (①4).
- **Flag: the pass is read only from a resolution of the same user.** Confirmed, and judged load-bearing (①3).
- **Not measured: a live multi-environment host with a real auth plugin.** Confirmed by reading that no `kernel-resolver` ships in this repository; the identity step the new pins run is the real one and the stub-resolver host through `dispatch()` is the right instrument, as the #31396 record accepted. Accepted.
- **Hand-back verification claims** (red-first 2 failed | 253 passed against `main`'s blob, restored 263/263 with #31396's file, runtime suite 561 files / 9007 tests, tsc 0, eslint 0, 67/67 derived gates with one re-run after the module-top import): consistent with my reading of the tree; not reproduced; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts.
- **Row ⑩-b (out of scope, not done).** One pre-existing observation on a path outside this PR, read in the cited code and confirmed; not opened or widened by this PR. **Escalated** as its own private item in this series, together with the design question the hand-back raises for it; details stay off GitHub under the disclosure ruling.
- No open question in the hand-back is left unanswered.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing was read against the published spec on `main` and the live code, and the gate was pushed on every caller shape that reaches it.

- **Does it take a declared capability away at the consumer?** No. The declared capability is the membership gate; its pass is declared for members of the platform organization; and the organization a session principal acts in is the one its resolution answers, the fact every other door already reads. A session caller whose resolution answers no organization is judged for membership in the environment, the same remedy every other caller has. For a member of the platform organization the resolution answers that organization (the vetting rule answers the claim or nothing, never a different organization), so no legitimate member's answer moves.
- **Does it make the spec's own refusal real?** Yes. The gate now reads the one answer the repository publishes for every door, and the dispatcher no longer holds a second answer to "which organization is this session in".
- **Shapes tried.** Each tenancy posture (`single`, `group`, `isolated`) and a host with no `tenancy` service; a member of the platform organization under each; a session whose user differs from the resolution's, and a request whose resolution is the guest envelope (nothing read, judged); a request carrying both a cookie and an API key, and a cookie beside a verified OAuth token on `/mcp` (the bearer arms decide, unchanged); a cookie beside a bearer the token door does not verify on `/mcp` (nit N2); an impersonation session (both reads name the same user; attribution only); a single-environment host and `api.enforceProjectMembership: false` (return before the arm); the fail-open when the gate's own session read throws (reached before the new arm, unchanged); the positive-membership cache (never seeded by the pass); the fallback seam outside `dispatch()` (out of scope, ③). None reaches past the gate after this PR in a way the contract does not allow; detail kept off this record under the disclosure ruling.
- **Should-fix S1** (`http-dispatcher.ts` 1635-1641): the comment block above the arms still ends "A session principal is judged by the session read above, as before." Two lines below it the new `else` reads the session principal's organization from the resolution, so that sentence now describes the user only. Reword it to say the session read names the user and the resolution names the organization, so the block agrees with the arm it introduces. No behaviour change.
- **Should-fix S2** (landing, see ②): squash, with the squash body free of the first commit's contrast.
- **Nit N1** (pins): no pin runs the real identity step on a host without a tenancy wall to show the pass holds for a session there; the unit pin hands the resolution in by hand. No effect on correctness or the contract.
- **Nit N2** (`/mcp`): a request carrying a session cookie beside a bearer the token door does not verify resolves as the guest, so the session caller is now judged here before the MCP domain answers; it is refused either way, and only the refusal's shape can move. No capability; a line in the arm's comment would record it.
- No must-fix.
